findings.title: No license file
remediation: Add a LICENSE file with the full text of the license you chose.

citations.note: no license file at the repository root

findings.title: SQL built from strings
findings.description: `find_user` in app.py formats values into the SQL passed to `conn.execute()`.
remediation: Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute("... WHERE id = %s", (user_id,)).
For dynamic identifiers, choose from an allow-list instead of formatting input in.

citations.snippet: return conn.execute(f"SELECT id, email FROM users WHERE name = '{name}'").fetchone()

findings.title: Command built for a shell
findings.description: `export_report` in app.py runs a computed command through a shell (`subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`).
remediation: Pass an argument list without a shell: subprocess.run(["tool", arg], check=True).
Validate arguments against an allow-list; never interpolate them into a command string.

findings.title: Unsafe deserialization
findings.description: `load_session` in app.py deserializes with `pickle.loads()`, which can execute code embedded in the data.
remediation: Use a data-only format (JSON) for anything that crosses a trust boundary.
For YAML use yaml.safe_load or Loader=yaml.SafeLoader.

findings.title: Dynamic code execution
findings.description: `calculate` in app.py passes a runtime value to `eval()`.
remediation: Replace eval with a parser for the expected format (json.loads, ast.literal_eval, a lookup table).
If dynamic code is truly required, never pass it data that crosses a trust boundary.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.description: The final stage of Dockerfile (from line 3) never sets USER, so it runs as root.
remediation: Create a system user in the image and add USER <name> before the entrypoint.

findings.title: README has no install or usage section
findings.description: README.md has 1 heading(s) and none covers installing, running or using the project.
remediation: Add an Install / Quickstart section with copy-pasteable commands.

findings.title: Network or database call inside a loop
findings.description: `fetch_avatars` in app.py calls `requests.get()` inside a loop: one round trip per iteration.
remediation: Batch the work: one query with IN (...), a bulk API, or prefetching related rows.
If calls must stay separate, run them concurrently with a bounded pool.

findings.title: Blocking call inside async code
findings.description: `send_email` in app.py is `async` but calls the blocking `requests.post()`.
remediation: Use the async equivalent (asyncio.sleep, an async HTTP client, asyncio.create_subprocess_exec).
Or move the blocking call to a worker thread with asyncio.to_thread.

findings.title: Raw HTML sink
findings.description: web/render.js:6 assigns computed markup to innerHTML/outerHTML.
remediation: Set textContent, or render through the framework's escaping.
If HTML is required, sanitize it with a maintained sanitizer (for example DOMPurify).

findings.title: async callback passed to forEach
findings.description: web/render.js:10 passes an async callback to forEach.
remediation: Use for...of with await, or await Promise.all(items.map(async ...)).

findings.title: Unpinned base image
findings.description: Dockerfile:3 builds FROM `python:latest` without a fixed version.
remediation: Pin an explicit version tag, ideally with an @sha256 digest.

findings.title: MD5 or SHA-1 hash
remediation: Use hashlib.sha256 (or blake2b) for integrity, and bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 for passwords.
If the hash is not security-relevant, pass usedforsecurity=False to make that explicit.

findings.title: Awaits run one at a time in a loop
findings.description: `notify` in app.py awaits `send_email` once per loop iteration, one after another.
remediation: Collect the coroutines and await them together (asyncio.gather or a TaskGroup) with a concurrency limit.

findings.title: Unpinned dependency
findings.description: requirements.txt lists 2 requirement(s) without an exact `==` version.
remediation: Pin exact versions in application manifests, or commit a lockfile.
Let a bot (Dependabot, Renovate) propose upgrades as reviewable changes.

findings.title: Deep clone through JSON
remediation: Use structuredClone(x).

findings.title: Every lookup opens a new SQLite connection and never closes it
findings.description: find_user creates a connection per call and returns without closing it, so busy endpoints leak file handles and pay connection setup on every request.
remediation: Open one connection per request (or use a pool) and close it in a finally block or with a context manager.
Add a test that calls find_user in a loop and checks open file descriptors.

findings.title: Report export lets callers write archives of arbitrary paths
findings.description: report_name flows unchecked into both the archive name and the source directory, so ../ sequences reach outside reports/. (This citation's line numbers are deliberately wrong to show drift detection.)
remediation: Accept only report names that match ^[a-z0-9-]+$.
Build the paths with pathlib and reject anything that resolves outside reports/.

findings.title: Session tokens are compared with a timing-unsafe equality check
findings.description: A planted hallucination: neither the file nor the code exists, so the verifier must flag it.
remediation: Use hmac.compare_digest for token comparison.
